title: Why does the Qur'an honor parents with a word that usually means humiliation?

beats.narration: The Qur'an tells you to treat your parents with a word that usually means humiliation. Why?
This verse says: lower for them the wing of lowliness. That word is dhull — elsewhere it means being brought genuinely low, even humiliated. Translators soften it. The text doesn't.
Now watch the wing. Elsewhere a prophet is told: lower your wing to those who follow you. The strong one spreads a wing over the weak, the way a bird shelters its young.
Here the figure turns over. The child once sheltered now lowers the wing. The most we can fairly say: real tenderness asks the strong to be willingly brought low.
